chunks: Ibn Mahboub said: Nuh Abu Al-Yaqzan narrated to us from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:
Supplicate with this supplication: O Allah, I ask You by Your Mercy which cannot be attained from You except by Your Pleasure,

and the exiting from all Your disobedience, and the entering into everything that pleases You, and salvation from every predicament, and the exit from every major sin that I committed deliberately, or slipped by me in error, or insinuated upon me by the whispers of Satan.

I ask You for a fear that stops me at the limits of Your Pleasure, and by which every lustful desire insinuated by my whims is diverted from me, and my opinion is made to falter so that it does not exceed the boundary of Your permissibles.
I ask You, O Allah, for taking hold of the best of what You know, and leaving the evil of all that You know, or my mistakes from where I do not know, or from where I do know.

I ask You for expansion in sustenance, and asceticism in sufficiency, and the exit from every doubt through clarity, and correctness in every argument, and truthfulness in all situations, and fairness of people towards myself regarding what is against me or for me.
and humility in giving the due right from all situations of anger and pleasure, and leaving both little and much of rebellion in my speech and action.
and the completion of Your blessings in all things, and gratitude to You for them, so that You may be pleased, and after being pleased.
And I ask You for the choice in everything where there is a choice, among the easy matters, all of them, not the difficult ones. O Generous, O Generous, O Generous.
And open for me the door of the matter in which is health and relief, and open its door for me, and ease its exit for me.

And whoever of Your creatures You have empowered over me, seize him from me by his hearing, his sight, his tongue, and his hand; seize him from his right, his left, behind him, and in front of him, and prevent him from reaching me with evil.
Mighty is Your neighbor, and Majestic is the praise of Your Face, and there is no god but You. You are my Lord, and I am Your servant.
O Allah, You are my hope in every distress, and You are my reliance in every difficulty, and You are for me in every matter that befalls me a trust and a provision.
So how many worries weaken the heart, in which strategy is scarce, the enemy gloats over, and matters exhaust one.
I present them to You and complain of them to You, hoping to You in them from besides You, so You relieve them and suffice for them.
So You are the Guardian of every blessing, and the Owner of every need, and the End-point of every wish. To You is abundant praise, and to You is overflowing favor.
ai.seo_question: What is the supplication for all needs and distress in Shia tradition?
ai.summary: Recorded in *Al-Kafi* by Shaykh al-Kulayni, this supplication (Dua) serves as a comprehensive spiritual toolkit for navigating worldly and otherworldly needs, emphasizing the transition from self-reliance to total dependence on Allah. It uniquely integrates theological concepts of *khawf* (fear) as a stabilizing force against desire and requests for *khayrah* (divine choice) in matters where human judgment may be limited. The text reflects the Shia emphasis on *tawassul* through divine attributes, framing distress as an opportunity to deepen reliance on God's sufficiency (*kafa'ah*).

en.hubeali: Ibn Mahboub said, ‘Nuh Abu Al Yaqzan narrated to us,

(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said: ‘Supplicate with this supplication, ‘O Allah<sup>azwj</sup>! I ask You<sup>azwj</sup> by Your<sup>azwj</sup> Mercy which cannot be attained from You<sup>azwj</sup> except by Your<sup>azwj</sup> Pleasure,

and the exiting from the entirety of Your<sup>azwj</sup> disobedience, and the entering into every thing what Pleases You<sup>azwj</sup>, and the salvation from every predicament, and the exiting from every major sin indulged in by me deliberately, or an error by me as a mistake, or there was a faltering with it upon by by the insinuations of the Satan<sup>la</sup>’.

I ask You<sup>azwj</sup> for the fear which I could stop with upon the limits of Your<sup>azwj</sup> Pleasure, and I can diverge by it from every lustful desire insinuated by my desires, and my opinions would falter by it to exceed the Limit if Your<sup>azwj</sup> Permissibles.

I ask You<sup>azwj</sup>, O Allah<sup>azwj</sup>, for my taking with the good deeds what You<sup>azwj</sup> Know of and neglecting of my evil deeds all of which You<sup>azwj</sup> Know of, or my mistakes from where I do not (even) know of, or from where I do know of.

I ask You<sup>azwj</sup> of the Expansion in the sustenance, and the ascetism in the subsistence, and the coming out from every confusion by the clarity, and the correctness in every argument, and the truthfulness in the entirety of the places, and being fair with the people from myself regarding whatever is against me or for me,

and the subservience in the giving of the justice from the entirety of the situations, the anger and the pleasures, and neglecting the lesser rebellions and its more, in the words from me and the deeds,

and the completion of Your<sup>azwj</sup> Bounties in the entirety of the things, and the thanking to You<sup>azwj</sup> upon it, perhaps You<sup>azwj</sup> would be Pleased, and after the Pleasure (as well).

And I ask You<sup>azwj</sup> of the goodness during everythin what is to happen wherein is the goodness with the easy matters, all of them, not by its difficult ones. O Benevilent! O Benevolent! O Benevolent!
And Open a door of the matter for me in which is the good health, and the relief; and Open its door for me, and Ease its exit for me.

And the one from Your<sup>azwj</sup> creatures for whom You<sup>azwj</sup> have Empowered upon me, so Seize him from me by his hearing, and his sight, and his tongue, and his hands, and Seize him from his right, and from his left, and from behind him, and from his front, and Prevent him from arriving to me with evil.

Mighty is Your<sup>azwj</sup> Vicinity, and Majestic is Your<sup>azwj</sup> Laudation of Your<sup>azwj</sup> Face, and there is no God apart from You<sup>azwj</sup> my Lord<sup>azwj</sup>, and I am Your<sup>azwj</sup> servant.

O Allah<sup>azwj</sup>! You<sup>azwj</sup> are my hope in every distress, and You<sup>azwj</sup> are my reliance in every difficulty, and You<sup>azwj</sup> are a Reliable one and One can count upon during every matter which descends with me.
So how many worries has my heart been weakend from, and the strategies were scarce with regards to it, and the enemies gloated regarding it, and the matters exhausted me during it.

I present them with You<sup>azwj</sup> and complain of it to You<sup>azwj</sup>, hoping to You<sup>azwj</sup> regarding it from the ones besides You<sup>azwj</sup>, so You<sup>azwj</sup> Relieve it and Suffice for it,

for You<sup>azwj</sup> are the Guardian of every Bounty, and Owner of every need, and End-point of every wish. So for You<sup>azwj</sup> is the abundant Praise, and for You<sup>azwj</sup> is the (Giving of) extra Favours’.
en.sarwar: Ibn Mahbub has said that Nuh ibn Yaqdan has narrated from abu ’ Abd Allah (a.s.) who has said the following: “Say this prayer, ‘O Lord, I plead before You for Your favor that cannot be achieved except with Your happiness, for (Your help to) come out of all disobedience that cannot happen without Your approval, for (Your help to) enter into all that makes You happy, for safety from all dangers, for departure from all major sins that have happened from me, willingly or have slipped out mistakenly, or have passed in my mind due to satanic induction.

“I plead before You to place fear in me that can keep me within the limits of Your approval, shatter away from me all lustful evil thoughts that have passed in my desires, that have made my opinion slip away to crossover Your lawful limits.
I plead before You, O Lord, to take the best that You know, and ignore all the evil that You find or mistakes that I had no knowledge of or did have the knowledge thereof.

“I plead before You for increased sustenance, restraining to suffice with basic needs, coming out of confusing conditions with clearly stated instructions, correctness in evidence, truth in all circumstances, yielding to justice for people against or for my soul, dealing humbly in yielding to justice in all circumstances of anger and contentment, avoiding small or greater degrees of transgression in my words or deeds, completion of Your bounties in all things, and thankfulness to You for it so You are content with happiness.
“I plead before You for guidance in all the good choices wherein choices exist and are easy to achieve not that which is hard to achieve.
O Magnanimous, O Magnanimous, O Magnanimous, open for me the door to the fact in which there is well being (of the body and spirit) and relief, open for me its door and ease it off to leave.

If You may determine for any of Y our creatures to overpower me then hold and seize him by his hearing, his eyes, tongue, and hand, seize him from his right, left, behind, front and before him and prevent him from reaching me with evil.

Your neighbor is well protected, glorious is the praise of Your face, and no one deserves to be worshipped except You. You are my Lord, and I am Your slave and servant. O Lord, You are my hope in all pains.
You are my hope in all hardships, in all troubles that befall me, on You I depend and Y ou are my resources.
How many are the pains that weaken the heart, diminish in it the means, bring rejoice for the enemy, and exhaust the resources.

I present them before You, complain to You against it, come to You of all things so You provide me relief and suffice me against it (such pains), thus, You are my benefactor of all the bounties with me, the appropriator of all of my needs, and the end of all of my desires.
All praise belongs to You a great deal and (I am) thankful to You in addition.’”
